plain: Two men, Silas Newton and Leo GeBauer, are said to have been treated unfairly and set up in a 1950s fraud trial in Colorado over a doodlebug, a gadget said to find oil or minerals underground. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb praises the author William Steinman, whose book on the reported saucer crash case known as Aztec draws on Colorado court records. In UAPGerb's account, Steinman went through those records and found how unfairly the two men were attacked. He also brings in the government scientist Vannevar Bush. A researcher named Scott Ramsey puts the trial in Denver in 1953 and names a Herman Flader. He says the case went through seven judges, and each one refused to hear it. Ramsey also mentions the writer Frank Scully. The point of telling it is that if the two men were framed, the saucer story tied to them looks less like a con.
